subject: Clarify SOC 2 scope: edge-connectors, non-prod routing and exception path
messages:
From: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@finexa.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: security@finexa.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 15:12:00 -0400
Subject: SOC 2 question: non-prod traffic via edge connectors

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off our SOC 2 Type II review and have a couple of nuanced routing questions that affect scope. High level: Finexa will be running integration tests from our non-prod environment that reach Redwood Dedicated pools through your edge connector layer. Some of that traffic will egress via public-facing NATs on the Dedicated side to reach 3rd-party monitoring endpoints (we're working on reducing that, but it's current state).

Two asks: 1) Will that non-prod traffic be considered "in-scope" for our SOC 2 assessment of the period 2026-07-01 → 2027-06-30 if it traverses your dedicated pools but exits via public egress? 2) We need the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (preferably the 2026 report) and, if scope doesn't line up, a bridge letter that explicitly calls out routing exceptions for non-prod.

Can you also provide a short list of evidence items we should collect (network diagram, tenant mapping, syslog retention, KMS ownership, etc.) so we can pass this to our auditor? I've attached our initial questionnaire to speed this up.

Attachments: finexa_initial_questionnaire.pdf (PDF)

Appreciate the help — we have a kickoff call with our auditor next Wednesday and want to confirm scope before then.

Best,
Alice
Security Program Manager
Finexa Corp
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@finexa.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2027 17:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question: non-prod traffic via edge connectors

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the questionnaire. Short answer up front: the path you described can pull the non-prod traffic into scope depending on two factors we need to confirm: (A) whether requests terminate on Dedicated tenant VMs only, or whether cross-pool routing/burst to hosted variants is possible for that workload, and (B) whether the egress path crosses shared-hosted infrastructure (NATs / public internet exits) managed by our hosted control plane.

To get you a definitive answer and a bridge letter if required, please send the following items (minimal set) before our auditor call: 1) a simple request flow diagram showing source environment → edge connector → pool type (dedicated identifier) → egress destination; 2) example source IPs or CIDR ranges used by your non-prod tests; 3) are you authenticating with customer-scoped API keys or using a shared account?; 4) expected volume / burst pattern during tests.

In parallel I'll loop in Jonas (runtime infra) and Kim (compliance) to describe how edge connectors and Dedicated pools are configured today and what evidence we can produce (network topology, tenant isolation proof, syslog retention screenshot, KMS ownership statement).

We also have our SOC 2 Type II 2026 report and a draft bridge letter template that covers limited routing/exceptions — I can deliver those once we confirm the routing matrix.

On timing: if you can send the flow diagram & sample IPs by Monday 8/30 we should be able to provide the SOC 2 report and bridge letter draft by Thursday 9/02.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, alice.meyer@finexa.com
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 09:10:00 +0200
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question: non-prod traffic via edge connectors

On Fri, 27 Aug 2027 at 17:05 Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com> wrote:
> In parallel I'll loop in Jonas (runtime infra) and Kim (compliance) to describe how edge connectors and Dedicated pools are configured today...

Thanks Hannah — adding some technical context so Alice and your auditor have concrete items to evaluate.

1) Architecture summary (short): Edge connectors are lightweight proxies that map incoming connections to a target pool. For Dedicated pools we enforce tenant isolation at the process/container level and per-pool network namespaces. By default, Dedicated pools can be configured with either (a) private egress via PrivateLink/VPC Peering (recommended) or (b) a managed public egress path that uses a pool-specific NAT gateway.

2) Scope implication: If your non-prod traffic terminates on Dedicated tenant instances and the egress stays within a pool-specific NAT (no cross-pool routing and no shared-hosted egress), that traffic is generally considered in-scope but scoped to the Dedicated deployment boundary (i.e., evidence will be tied to that Dedicated config). However, if Dedicated is configured to burst into our hosted shared capacity or if the egress traverses a shared-hosted NAT, then the hosted environment controls become relevant and your auditor will likely mark the traffic in-scope for the hosted environment too.

3) Evidence we can provide on short notice: - annotated network topology PNG (redwood_network_topology_v2.png) - dedicated pool tenant mapping export (CSV) - syslog retention policy excerpt (screenshot) - KMS key ownership statement & CMK ARNs - config export showing pool egress mode (private vs managed public)

4) Bridge letter guidance: If you want a minimal bridge letter, we can draft language that: (a) confirms your non-prod traffic terminated on Dedicated pool ID XYZ during the audit period, (b) lists the exact egress mode (pool-specific NAT vs PrivateLink), and (c) states which control domains are excluded/included for that traffic. That draft is attached as proposed_bridge_letter_draft.docx.

Action items for Finexa (to accelerate): share the flow diagram, sample IPs/CIDRs, and whether you currently use API keys scoped per-customer. If you prefer, we can change the Dedicated pool egress to PrivateLink for the duration of the tests (temporary config) to keep everything strictly within customer-managed VPC boundaries — we can treat that as a remediation to remove hosted egress from scope.

-Jonas
Senior Infra Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@finexa.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 question: non-prod traffic via edge connectors

Alice — thanks for the quick turn. Per Jonas' note and our compliance practice: we can provide the 2026 SOC 2 Type II PDF (attached) and a bridge letter that calls out the specific routing exception for your non-prod tests.

To confirm next steps and deliverables:
- You to send the one-page flow diagram + sample CIDRs by EOD Monday 2027-08-30.
- We'll deliver: (A) SOC 2 Type II 2026 PDF (soc2-typeii-2026-redwood.pdf), (B) proposed bridge letter (proposed_bridge_letter_draft.docx) with explicit language about Dedicated pool ID(s) and egress mode, and (C) annotated network topology (redwood_network_topology_v2.png) and tenant mapping export.

If you prefer we can also flip the pool egress to PrivateLink for your test window — that would remove hosted egress from the equation and simplify auditor sign-off. Let us know which you prefer.

I'll also include a short evidence checklist for your auditor:
- Network topology (annotated)
- Dedicated pool tenant mapping (CSV)
- Egress mode config screenshot (pool console)
- Syslog retention policy excerpt (screenshot)
- KMS key ownership statement (signed)
- Bridge letter (if audit period mismatch or routing exception)

We can get the package to you by 2027-09-02 if we get the diagram and CIDRs on Monday.

Thanks,
Hannah
Head of Security Programs
Redwood Inference
Attachments: soc2-typeii-2026-redwood.pdf, proposed_bridge_letter_draft.docx, redwood_network_topology_v2.png
